==English== {{wp}} ===Pronunciation=== * {{IPA|en|/ɹəˈvɛnd͡ʒ/|/ɹɪˈvɛnd͡ʒ/|/ɹiˈvɛnd͡ʒ/}} ** {{audio|en|en-us-revenge.ogg|a=US}} * {{IPA|en|/ɹəˈvendʒ/|a=AU}} * {{hyph|en|re|venge}} * {{rhymes|en|ɛndʒ|s=2}} ===Etymology 1=== From {{bor|en|frm|revenge}}, a derivation from {{m|frm|revenger}}, from {{der|en|fro|revengier}} (possibly influenced by {{der|en|pro|revènge||revenge, comeback}}, from {{cog|pro|revenir||to come back}}), a variant of {{cog|frm|revancher}} (whence deverbal {{cog|fr|revanche}}), from {{cog|fro|revenchier}}. The variants {{cog|fro|vengier}} (whence {{cog|fr|venger}}) and {{cog|fro|venchier}} are both descended from {{der|en|la|vindicō}}, with stress-conditioned different parallel development in the inflectional forms. {{doublet|en|revanche}}. Compare {{m|en|avenge}} and {{m|en|vengeance}}. ====Noun==== {{en-noun|-|s}} # Any form of [[personal]], [[retaliatory]] [[action]] against an [[individual]], [[institution]], or [[group#Noun|group]] for some [[alleged#Adjective|alleged]] or [[perceived #Adjective|perceived]] [[harm#Noun|harm]] or [[injustice]]. #: {{synonyms|en|payback|wreak|Thesaurus:revenge}} #: {{ux|en|They took '''revenge''' on their enemies.}} #: {{ux|en|Indifference is the sweetest '''revenge'''.}} #: {{ux|en|When I left my wife, she tried to set fire to the house in '''revenge'''.}} #: {{ux|en|After tearing his fave T-shirt unintentionally, my brother wreaked '''revenge''' on me by ripping my most prized blazer apart.}} #* {{RQ:en:CNN|author=Megan Thomas|title=Liam Neeson expresses regret for once contemplating racist revenge|url=https://www.cnn.com/2019/02/04/entertainment/liam-neeson-revenge|date=2019-02-04|passage=Liam Neeson has revealed that years ago he contemplated carrying out a racist '''revenge''' attack after someone close to him was raped.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20221006033031/https://edition.cnn.com/2019/02/04/entertainment/liam-neeson-revenge}} # A [[win#Noun|win]] by a previous [[loser]]. #* {{RQ:Ferguson Zollenstein|chapter=I|passage=“I'm through with all pawn-games,” I laughed. “Come, let us have a game of lansquenet. Either I will take a farewell fall out of you or you will have your sevenfold '''revenge'''”.}} #* {{quote-av |en |date=January 27, 1999 |title=w:Bride of Chaotica! |series={{w|Star Trek: Voyager}} |publisher=w:Paramount Domestic Television |genre=[[science fiction|Science Fiction]] |oclc=1375384954 |text=CHAOTICA: Arachnia, death as you know it has no hold on me. My defeat is but a temporary setback. I shall return to seek my '''revenge'''.
JANEWAY: He doesn't give up, does he?
PARIS: They never do.
CHAOTICA: Our love was not meant to be, my Queen. But be warned. You have not seen the last of (gurgle) Chaotica.}} =====Derived terms===== {{col|en|nonrevenge|prevenge|revengeance|revengeless|revengism|Montezuma's revenge |revenge buying |revengeful| revenge drama |revenge is a dish best served cold |revenge is sweet |revenge porn |revenge quitting|revenge quit |revenge shopping |revenge spending |revenge travel |revenge tragedy |Pharaoh's revenge }} =====Descendants===== * {{desc|ja|リベンジ|bor=1}} =====Translations===== {{trans-top|retaliatory action}} * Albanian: * Arabic: * Armenian: * Aromanian: * Assamese: * Asturian: * Azerbaijani: * Bashkir: * Basque: * Belarusian: * Bengali: * Bulgarian: * Carpathian Rusyn: * Catalan: * Chechen: * Cherokee: * Chinese: * Czech: * Danish: * Dutch: * Esperanto: * Estonian: * Ewe: * Faroese: * Finnish: * French: * Galician: * Georgian: * German: * Gothic: * Greek: * Hebrew: * Hindi: * Hungarian: * Icelandic: * Ido: * Indonesian: * Irish: * Italian: * Japanese: * Kapampangan: * Kazakh: * Korean: * Kurdish: * Kyrgyz: * Lao: * Latin: * Latvian: * Lithuanian: * Macedonian: * Malay: * Malayalam: * Māori: * Marathi: * Mongolian: * Norman: * Norwegian: * Occitan: * Old Church Slavonic: * Old English: * Ossetian: * Pashto: * Pennsylvania German: * Persian: * Plautdietsch: * Polish: * Portuguese: * Romanian: * Russian: {{t+|ru|месть|f}}, {{t+|ru|рева́нш|m}}, {{t+|ru|мще́ние|n}}, {{t+|ru|отмще́ние|n}}, {{t+|ru|воздая́ние|n}} * Scottish Gaelic: * Serbo-Croatian: * Sindhi: * Slovak: * Slovene: * Sorbian: * Spanish: * Swahili: * Swedish: * Tagalog: * Tajik: * Tatar: * Thai: * Turkish: * Ukrainian: * Urdu: * Uyghur: * Uzbek: * Vietnamese: * Walloon: * Welsh: * Yiddish: {{trans-bottom}} ===Etymology 2=== From {{inh|en|enm|revengen}}, from {{der|en|fro|revengier}}, {{m|fro|revenger}}. ====Verb==== {{en-verb}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[take revenge]] for (a particular [[harmful]] [[action]]) or on behalf of (its [[victim]]); to [[avenge]]. #: {{ux|en|Arsenal '''revenged''' their loss to Manchester United last time with a 5–0 drubbing this time.}} #* {{RQ:Dryden Aeneis|1|passage=The gods are just, and will '''revenge''' our cause.}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1814|author=w:Lord Berners|title=The Ancient Chronicles of Sir John Froissart |passage=to '''revenge''' the death of our fathers}} #* {{RQ:Hunt Seer|passage=However, my veneration for that illustrious man was so great, that on the night when he died, I '''revenged''' him finely on his two principal enemies.}} # {{lb|en|transitive|reflexive}} To take one's revenge (''on'' or ''upon'' someone). #: {{ux|en|We've finally '''revenged''' ourselves on our enemies.}} #* {{RQ:Shakespeare Julius Caesar|IV|iii|passage=Come, Antony, and young Octavius, come,
'''Revenge''' yourselves alone on Cassius.}} # {{lb|en|intransitive|archaic}} To take [[vengeance]]; to revenge itself. #* {{RQ:Shakespeare Henry 6-3|I|iv|passage=a bird that will '''revenge''' upon you all}} #* {{RQ:Dante Cary Vision|volume=III|canto=VII|page=30|lines=45–47|passage=Count it not hard henceforth, when thou dost hear
That a just vengeance was by righteous court
Justly '''reveng'd'''. {{...}}}} =====Derived terms===== {{col|en|revengeable|unrevenged|revengingly|unrevenging |revengement|revenger}} =====Translations===== {{trans-top|to take one's revenge on someone}} * Albanian: * Belarusian: * Bikol: * Bulgarian: * Catalan: * Comorian: * Czech: * Danish: * French: * Galician: * Malayalam: * Mongolian: * Tagalog: * Turkish: * Ukrainian: {{trans-bottom}} {{trans-top|to take revenge for an action}} * Arabic: * Belarusian: * Bikol: * Bulgarian: * Burmese: * Catalan: * Chinese: * Czech: * Danish: * Dutch: * Finnish: * French: * German: * Greek: * Hindi: * Italian: * Japanese: * Korean: * Lao: * Macedonian: * Malayalam: * Norwegian: * Old Church Slavonic: * Persian: * Polish: * Portuguese: * Romanian: * Russian: {{t+|ru|мстить|impf}}, {{t+|ru|отомсти́ть|pf}} * Serbo-Croatian: * Slovak: * Slovene: * Swedish: * Tajik: * Thai: * Ukrainian: * Vietnamese: {{trans-bottom}} {{trans-top|to take revenge on an actor}} * Belarusian: * Bikol: * Catalan: * Czech: * Greek: * Irish: * Lao: * Macedonian: * Portuguese: * Romanian: * Russian: {{t+|ru|мстить|impf}}, {{t+|ru|отомсти́ть|pf}} * Thai: * Ukrainian: {{trans-bottom}} ===See also=== * {{l|en|vendetta}} * {{l|en|avenge}} * {{l|en|venge}} * {{l|en|vengeance}} * {{l|en|get one's own back}} * {{l|en|get back at}} somebody * {{l|en|retaliate}} * {{l|en|revanche}} ===Anagrams=== * {{anagrams|en|a=eeegnrv|genever}}
